title: Chartered Accountant

steps: CA Foundation (after Class 12, or provisional registration after Class 10)
2–3 years articleship at a CA firm
path.note: Many take longer because of failed attempts.

rows.label: Articleship
rows.value: Low stipend (fixed by ICAI/firm; much lower than a salary)

rows.label: Newly qualified CA (ICAI campus, Apr–May 2026)
rows.value: Average ~₹13 LPA; highest domestic offer ₹27.5 LPA; international offers higher

pros: Strong, respected qualification; at the 2026 ICAI campus drive there were ~8,900 vacancies for ~5,800 candidates
Good starting pay for the cost of the course (far cheaper than an MBA or private engineering)
Paths into Big 4, banking, corporate finance, or your own practice
cons: Brutal exams: the Foundation pass rate is about 1 in 5; repeated attempts are common and demoralising
Articleship is long, low-paid and often heavy on grunt work
Audit and tax-season crunches (long nights before filing deadlines)
AI and automation are changing routine bookkeeping and audit work

competitionReality.signal: ~10 lakh students registered with ICAI (2025 report)
competitionReality.reality: CA Foundation pass rate ~19–21% per attempt

sceneIdeas: The night before the GST filing deadline
A client hands you a shoebox of receipts
Failing one group of CA Inter by 4 marks
Your articleship boss asks you to stay late again
Spotting something odd in a client's books
